title: Rapid Promotion
paragraphs: After seeing Father off, I turned my gaze toward Filo-chan. Just then, Filo-chan scampered off into her room.
“Anyone other than the guy with the spear! Let’s sleep with Filo!”
“Boo…”
“Yeah, I guess so.”
Hmph… I have no idea what that Lazy Pig just said. And so, after seeing Father off, we ended up staying home to mind the house.
Since we’re not allowed to go out, there’s not much to do—I’m bored. So I’m setting up a chair in front of the room Filo-chan went into and waiting.
It brings back memories. It reminds me of that night when I first realized Filo-tan’s love for me… that day when I waited with bated breath for Father and the others to come out.
“Um… Spear Hero, what are you doing?”

My older sister, who’d decided to wait until Father returned, came over and asked me that. At first, she was doing push-ups and pull-ups… but I guess that training is over now? Lately, it seems she’s been helping Father with his peddling business, working on things like processing monster materials.

Come to think of it, I’ve heard that when she has some free time during her peddling trips, she’s been doing that sort of work. As for her magic training, that’s also been coming along quite well lately. Father has mastered the script I translated and is starting to get the hang of magic as well. Big Sister-in-law, thanks to her Older Sister, was able to pick it up quickly.
“I’m standing by so I can protect Filo-tan at any moment.”
The nature of this loop is still shrouded in mystery. You never know when or what might happen.

Oh? I hear some commotion coming from inside the room—is everything all right? I’ve been told not to go in, so I can’t. I got scolded the last time I tried to peek in. My Older Sister is heading into the room. Should I listen in?
“There’s a guy with a spear standing right outside the room!?”
“I’m not going in on Lord Naofumi’s orders… so please be patient.”
“Yaaah!”
“Filo, if you throw too many tantrums, it’ll end badly again. So please stay calm…”
“Ugh…”
I wonder what’s going on? Could it be that? Maybe she’s anxious because Father isn’t here. But don’t worry. I’ll protect her from any misfortune! Soon, the young lady came out of the room.
“Spear Hero, could you please step away from here?”
“That’s impossible. I’m The Love Hunter, after all. While Father’s away, I have a duty to rush to Filo-tan’s aid whenever she’s in danger.”
“So you’re a hunter in the sense that you’re biding your time…”
Older Sister let out a deep sigh. I’m not quite sure what she means by that. What exactly do you mean by ‘waiting for an opportunity’?
“Please try not to disturb Filo’s peaceful sleep, okay?”
“Of course!”

I’m here to protect Filo-tan—I have no intention of harming her. In fact, it’s no exaggeration to say I’m here to eliminate anything that might harm her. With that, Big Sister went back inside. Time is ticking away, tick-tock, tick-tock.

Ah… Just knowing I can be near Filo-chan makes this a joyful time. I can’t see Filo-chan, but just imagining what she might be doing inside the room gets my heart racing. Is she sleeping soundly, or is she standing by the window with a melancholy expression, gazing up at the night sky until Father returns? I won’t know what’s going on inside until I check. Hehe, isn’t that just the way it is?

Such a delightful time passed in the blink of an eye, and just as the morning mist began to drift in… Father and the others returned. They quietly opened the front door and came inside. It’s a considerate gesture Father makes unconsciously toward those still asleep. Being able to show such small acts of thoughtfulness is one of the wonderful things about Father. However, it seems some people—starting with Big Sister and Lazy Pig—were already awake and waiting.
“I’m home.”
“Welcome back, Naofumi-sama, Sadeena-nee-san.”
“Welcome back, Father.”

I waited until I was sure Father had returned before stepping away from the door to Filo-tan’s room to greet him. By the way, according to the villagers who slept beside her (I’m jealous), it seems Filo-tan was moaning in her sleep. If it was a scary dream, shouldn’t they have woken her up? When I mentioned that later, they replied that even after she woke up, it turned out to be a nightmare. What kind of nightmare was that, anyway? I’ll go kick the cause’s ass!
“Oof.”

The Lazy Pig asks Father with a yawn. Father brought a bunch of steamed buns—probably bought at a night market—as a gift and plopped them down on the table with a thud. Looks like one per person, doesn’t it? If I give my share to Filo-chan, will that boost her favorability toward me?
“Ah, it was exactly as I mentioned on the way here. However, the bad news involved a high-profile incident. Zeltoble sure is getting dangerous.”
“What do you mean?”
My Older Sister asks.

“Apparently, a powerful The Slave Trader in Zeltoble—who was a Rival to another The Slave Trader—was found murdered. Since he held considerable power, they’re keeping this under wraps for now and will make it public once the aftermath has been handled.”

That’s what Father said. Apparently, around this evening, a merchant who had built a grand mansion in Zeltoble was found brutally murdered inside his estate. This merchant was said to be extremely cautious, employing dozens of renowned mercenaries as his bodyguards. It seems even those bodyguards met the same fate. Since this incident involved a well-known merchant with a large retinue of guards being brutally murdered by the perpetrator in a short amount of time, it sent shockwaves through the Guild of Darkness, leading to this emergency meeting where information was shared.
“He must have made quite a few enemies, didn’t he?”
“Boo.”
“Well… I’ve heard the rumors too, and they’re not exactly flattering. Still, they say he was straightforward when it came to money and had a fair amount of generosity.”

“That’s only natural. Without that kind of character, he wouldn’t have been the sort of person to command respect in Zeltoble. Anyway, I’ve heard I’ve been chosen to fill his shoes—or rather, to take his vacant position…”
Oh, what a huge promotion. I suppose that means the “Class Up Festival” will be held as planned.

“I can’t shake the feeling that The Slave Trader, the Jewelry Merchant, and Elena’s family all played a part in this… but I’m not about to pass up the opportunity. Starting tomorrow, I can Class Up as much as I want.”
What a lightning-fast promotion. As expected, Father is a man who makes a fortune doing business in Zeltoble. I’ll follow him for the rest of my life!
“Anyway, enough about me—let’s get back to the topic at hand. It’s about that murdered merchant—the circumstances are rather puzzling.”
“Puzzling?”
“Yeah. For a murder motivated by a grudge, there’s hardly any sign of animosity in the way he was killed; yet, for a robbery, almost none of the precious metals or money were stolen.”
“So you’re saying it wasn’t a personal vendetta or a robbery—someone just stormed into a mansion guarded by armed mercenaries and killed the merchant?”
“That’s exactly what’s so strange, which is why we held a meeting within the Darkness Guild. There’s a possibility similar crimes could happen again.”

It could happen to any of us tomorrow. So the merchants are living in fear of this mysterious killer, I see. At the very least, as long as they’re operating here in Zeltoble, they’ve inevitably incurred the grudge of someone, to a greater or lesser extent. After all, this is the Darkness Guild we’re talking about.

“According to merchants who know the darkness of the world, the method resembles the way people are killed when rounded up by knightly orders from other nations. I suppose you could call it a ‘routine killing’? But if knights were behind it, we’d know who did it.”

Knights are the state’s lackeys, after all. The moment they get involved, it means all the relevant authorities are already on the case. Father seems to believe there’s no way the Dark Guild wouldn’t have picked up on those movements. Then, for some reason, Father looked at me.
“What is it?”
“Well… Motoyasu is out of the question. He was fooling around around here around the time of the crime, and even if he were the culprit, he wouldn’t kill someone like that.”

That’s right. After all, there’s no reason to kill a merchant. Unless they’d committed some barbaric act—like hurting Father or Filo-chan during a loop—I wouldn’t go so far as to kill them. Merchants are a valuable resource, second only to bandits in terms of wealth. Killing them would serve no purpose.

Even if I were to kill someone, I wouldn’t leave any evidence behind. I’d either make them vanish with a Brionac or blow them to bits with a Burst Lance. Or I’d annihilate just their souls, leaving them as empty shells. With any of these three methods, there’d be no evidence in the form of a corpse.
“That’s a pretty unpleasant way to be trusted.”
“I’m innocent, you know.”
“I sense madness in the fact that your first words are ‘I’m innocent.’”
Father and Lazy Pig both let out a sigh. What’s the matter? I’m doing my very best with all my heart and soul! I just want you to understand that much, at least.
“I briefly considered the possibility that Motoyasu might use Skills to create a doppelganger and kill a merchant to further my career…”
“I’ll do it if necessary.”

“Don’t. There’s absolutely no need to resort to such tactics. Once this is all settled, I’ll have unlimited use of the Dragon Hourglass anyway, and making money is just a strategic move for the future. I have no intention of settling at the top of Zeltoble.”

After all, Father is a man whose sole purpose is to save the world from the Waves. I suppose he’s decided that once he can fully utilize the title of “Hero,” his status in Zeltoble will no longer be necessary.
“Speaking of which, can you create a duplicate of yourself?”
“I have no recollection of possessing such skills.”
If I did, I could take down even a strengthened Spirit Tortoise all by myself. Unfortunately, I don’t have those skills.
“Then don’t say it!”
Father got angry at me. I was just answering honestly.

“I was almost suspected myself, but I managed to cover it up in various ways—after all, there’s no merchant who doesn’t have something up his sleeve. As expected, no one made the mistake of jumping to conclusions without concrete evidence.”
Father flashes an evil grin. He looks like he’s having a lot of fun. Big Sister looks worried.
“Um… so, Naofumi-sama, is there something in particular that’s bothering you?”
“Well, yes. Judging by this modus operandi, it feels similar to the tree Itsuki was talking about. Motoyasu, does this ring a bell?”

Asked by Father, I think back over my memories so far. Itsuki loves heroes, after all. It’s not entirely impossible that he’d use a method like this—killing unscrupulous merchants in secret. He later told us himself that in the first world and in the loops where we weren’t part of his group, he went around taking down corrupt nobles. But…
“If Itsuuki were around, I think he’d use his authority as a hero to arrest merchants who were up to no good, don’t you think? ‘Actually, I was a hero all along!’—that’s Itsuuki’s style, after all.”
“I see…”

I think that method is far too cruel for Itsuki. He’s a kid who loves justice, after all. I can’t imagine him doing anything that would make him look bad to others. Not to sound harsh, but there’s something a bit idealistic about Itsuki’s sense of justice. He’s a self-proclaimed champion of justice who ignores the fact that there are hopelessly evil entities in this world.

“Well, as for the investigation files—or rather, the fact that the slaves, their records, and the contract documents are currently missing—that’s a bit of a cause for concern. But since Sadeena says none of the villagers were involved, I suppose we’ll have to accept that.”
“So, did he kill The Slave Trader and steal the slaves?”
“That’s how it looks. As things stand, it seems the goal was to steal valuable slaves.”

However, it seems there’s little to gain from this. At the very least, it’s hardly worth going so far as to kill a well-known merchant who belongs to the Darkness Guild. In fact, wouldn’t the downsides outweigh the benefits?
“As for the missing slaves, it seems some who were getting what they deserved were being sold as merchandise.”

This is what Father told me. Apparently, a certain spendthrift, fallen noble from a neighboring country of Zeltoble had been living a life of extravagant luxury, using his title, lands, and estate as collateral just to keep up appearances. He was raising money for his debts by imposing heavy taxes on his subjects, but due to factors like the economic downturn, he reportedly became unable to repay his debts. With no other choice, he tried to sell off his subjects, but the subjects reported him to the national auditors, exposing his crimes. As compensation, The Slave Trader took them away to settle the debt.

“Well, an arrest warrant has been issued for that fellow. Apparently, because of his ties to The Slave Trader, he’ll have to work off the debt. It also seems that female slaves, in particular, are disappearing at an alarming rate.”
“What about the male slaves?”
“Since they were used as bodyguards, they were all wiped out.”
Hmm… This is a rather fishy case. It’s the kind of story that’s bound to become gossip.

“…If you’re doing business in Zeltoble, a scoundrel like that might show up, so just be extra careful. As for the culprit, an independent investigation is already underway, so they’ll likely be identified soon.”
“Got it. Filo, Keel, and I will do our best to protect ourselves—not just from the waves, but from anything else as well.”
“That’s good. I’ve made quite a bit of money myself. I’ll devote the rest of this period to leveling up.”

So, the matter of Father’s promotion in Zeltoble has been pretty much settled. Now that we can do Class Up, the focus will shift to strengthening our characters. It feels like my spear is finally going to blaze with Fire to raise everyone’s levels.
